blindSummary: This federation of two small islands is part of its sub-region's decriminalisation wave (a 2022 court ruling); tiny population, tourist economy, no documented anti-trans violence pattern; no legal gender recognition.
blindOutOfScope: Thin data; inherits the regional profile.

Regional newspaper (Aug 2022): the sub-region's shared supreme court struck down anti-sodomy laws - the ruling covering this country (a named civil-society constitutional challenge) decriminalised consensual same-sex conduct.
An international rights organisation's index page of its UN advocacy submissions on this country - navigation/landing page only.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): decriminalised in 2022 via a civil-society constitutional challenge - two provisions of the offences-against-the-person act contravened constitutional privacy and expression rights; no legal gender recognition; no non-discrimination laws.

Presentation to a UN periodic review (UPR, 2025) by a national LGBTI organisation and a regional LGBTI alliance: decriminalisation in 2022 after civil-society court challenge; LGBTQ+ citizens included in the national gender-equality policy 2022-2027 but 'lack of tangible steps by the State'; discrimination in workplace, education, accommodation and hate speech still not illegal; LGBTQ+ people avoid law enforcement.
blindLocalsOnly: No legal gender recognition - a resident-facing gap.
blindTangential: The 2022 decriminalisation ruling removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
